result.finding: Assessed 5 CWE rules in Credentials & Secrets: 1 FOUND, 4 NOT_FOUND
evidence: Reviewed all runtime source/configuration, Docker/Compose, Oracle scripts, .env.example and credential-bearing documentation locations without copying values. CWE-259/321/798: runtime secrets supplied by environment or unresolved required property; BCrypt encoder, no embedded passwords or cryptographic key found. Documentation/example placeholders are not active credentials; default usernames alone do not constitute complete hard-coded credentials. CWE-732: runtime writes require authentication, public reads are intentional by documented design, Oracle scripts grant schema-scoped privileges rather than DBA; no demonstrated unintended resource permission assignment. Docker root execution noted but not treated alone as this CWE. CWE-778: no configured authentication event audit. Tests excluded from production vulnerability classification; no git-history secret scan and no deployed IAM/filesystem validation. Secret values and password examples omitted from reports.

values.name: Use of Hard-coded Password
values.description: The product contains a hard-coded password, which it uses for its own inbound authentication or for outbound communication to external components.

values.name: Use of Hard-coded Cryptographic Key
values.description: The product uses a hard-coded, unchangeable cryptographic key.

values.name: Incorrect Permission Assignment for Critical Resource
values.description: The product specifies permissions for a security-critical resource in a way that allows that resource to be read or modified by unintended actors.

values.name: Insufficient Logging

evidence.explanation: SecurityConfig configures HTTP Basic authentication but installs no authentication success/failure audit handler or event listener. Authentication rejection occurs in Spring Security before HomeController/DetailController log calls; no application authentication-event listener or access-log configuration exists. In the Docker profile Spring web logs are WARN and Spring Security has no explicit audit logging configuration. Thus unsuccessful login attempts lack an application-configured security audit record identifying the attempted user and outcome. This is absence of configured authentication auditing, not a claim that all application actions are unlogged; upload/delete outcomes are logged.

values.description: When a security-critical event occurs, the product either does not record the event or omits important details about the event when logging it.

values.name: Use of Hard-coded Credentials
values.description: The product contains hard-coded credentials, such as a password or cryptographic key.
